title: tool_contract
description: A callable tool's contract inside a bundle: tools/<name>/tool.json (plan.md 5.1 S5, 6.4). Check B7.

inputs.description: a JSON Schema for the input object

outputs.description: a JSON Schema for the output object

side_effects.description: reads_instrument: the tool reads a device and changes nothing; it reaches the device, so it runs through the runner like any tool, and it needs no safety value (B9)

opens_by.description: what opens the gate for this tool; absent means safety_values. execution_permission is for a tool that starts an engine or writes the agent's own files and touches no instrument: it opens where the bundle's envelope/execution_permission.json, a copy of the lab's confirmed permission, reaches an engine (the person, 2026-11-16, docs/ideas/20261116.md). A tool that changes an instrument opens only by safety values a person wrote (MP4). A tool that reaches the network may open by the permission only to install packages, from a source its contract names under installs_from and the bundle's permission lists under package_sources, or to read data, from hosts its contract names under fetches_from and the permission lists under data_sources (tasks/023).

installs_from.description: for a tool that reaches the network to install the agent's own packages: the installer and the channel it fetches from. Its gate opens by the execution permission only where the bundle's permission lists the same pair (B9).

host.description: a bare lower-case host name, matched by equality: no scheme, port, path or wildcard

fetches_from.description: for a tool that reaches the network to read data (an engine's example inputs, a published table, an archive): every host it reads from, and how. Its gate opens by the execution permission only where the bundle's permission lists each host under data_sources with the same access (B9, tasks/023). A tool may name this beside installs_from; each is judged against its own list.
